links.reason: Line 4 யான்விளைத்த வினைப்பயன் is a real karma statement, but the kid's verse is flagged uncertain and the 'fallen state' reading is open; verse 35 is a general whirling-of-births claim (கறங்கென வினையினோடி), so the pair is the same doctrine twice, not 'borne out in the king's own case'.

331 repeats the very gesture of 306: தலை திறந்திட்டு (306 l.3) and நிதி தலை திறந்து (331 l.2), with the gold mountain (பொன் குன்றம் / செம் பொன் குன்று). The unsent order of the burning ground is in effect carried out for the child, and திருமகன் பெற்று எனச் makes the stranger's belief that he has a son plain.
links.text_issue: 331 line 4 (செருநிலம் பயப்பு உற) is unclear as printed

links.reason: Both verses use fire as a stratagem, but 141 names no Yugi and no stage-craft: it shows the king believing the burnt ornaments (நெருப்பிடை விழுந்தமை). 'His habit' rests on plot outside the verse; the fire in 110 frees the king, in 141 fakes a death, so the shared image is thin.

554 has the king say he will not yield though kings with a sea of an army fall at his feet (வேற்கடற் றானை வேந்தர்); 813 has கடற்படை உடைந்தது. கடல்-of-army is a stock figure, and 'turns a figure of speech into fact' is the note's gloss, since the kings in 813 are suitors in battle, not the figure's referent fulfilled.

Both are apologies for plain words, but the images differ (gem-bundle cloth, lamp with smoke) and 'AGREES' teaches only the shared convention; the note says only that the lamp is 'the same plea'. NKK 3 is also flagged uncertain.

695 says the minister will show a trick to enrage him and send him into the lion (மாயங் காட்டி உளைவித்து ... சீயந் தன்மேற் கொளப்புணர்த்திடுவன்); 696 carries it out: அரிகேது என்னும் விஞ்சையனைக் கூவி ... மாயச் சீய மாகென வகுத்து விட்டான். The later verse fulfils the plan and names the instrument.

Both use a driver and a vehicle for kingship, and 2909 adds ஊர்நிலம் அறிதல் தேற்றாது ஊருமேல், so the teaching is true. But PN 185 already carries the driver's skill (உய்த்தல் தேற்றான்), and the epic cannot add a condition to it; 'the epic belongs to an old comparison' is a claim of dependence the Tamil does not show.

2624 and NL 1 both set one who ate well against begging, but the epic names the cause, வெவ்வினை, and the Naladiyar names none; the note's 'qualifies' is not a limit on the quatrain. 'Teaches' is the shared theme of wealth's loss, and the epic gains nothing from the quatrain.

கேவலம் here is one word with two doctrines: the Jain full knowledge as bride (கேவலப் பெண்) and Saiva kevala as the soul's first bound state (கேவலத்தாரது விட்டவர்). Different schools, same word, no claim about one thing; this is not a tension, and 'gains' on the epic side names nothing a Jain verse lacks.
links.text_issue: both verses flagged uncertain; TM 494 reading is loose

links.reason: Both rest on the case of the beneficiary's flesh being eaten, but 196 shows only the brahmins eating (தின்றனர்) and blessing; the kid's identity is in the next verse, so 'the dead eat the dead' is not in this verse. It illustrates Kural 259's point (உயிர்செகுத்து உண்ணாமை) rather than qualifying it.

The shared image is a rutting elephant that kills its goad-men and breaks its post (பாகரும் கொன்றிட / கோலோர்க் கொன்று ... கந்துநீத்து), but it is a stock set piece. The teaching about two stages of mastery rests on 1839, which the packet does not show, and 'gains' on both sides is influence or story the Tamil does not display.

The words பறித்து நக்கான் in 2290 and பறியா நகும் in 774 are the same deed, yet the Kural already supplies the laugh's cause (spent his spear on an elephant, finds another in his body), so 'the couplet leaves it open' is untrue. The account of 2289 is outside this packet.

KN 19 has மராஅம் ... நாஞ்சில் வலவன் நிறம்போல and the heart gone ahead (நெடுவிடைச் சென்றதென் னெஞ்சு); TN 96 has the moonlight as the elder brother's pale colour (தம்முன் ... ஆய்நிறம்) and a spear (வேல்போலும்) to those lacking a partner. The same god's colour calls the returning man home and wounds the waiting woman, which the pair shows and neither alone.

1210 sends the envoys off though they brought evil words (தீதுரை கொணர்ந்து நஞ் செவிகள் சுட்ட) and says their fault is to be borne (பிழைத்தது பொறுக்கல்), where Kural 685 asks the envoy to drop what offends (தூவாத நீக்கி). The epic gives the case where the ideal fails and custom still protects.

Kural 1263 has the woman say she lives longing for his return; it names his resolve as companion (உள்ளம் துணையாக), but no grievance. KN 7's friend gives giving and crushing foes as the cause of his going, and the rain's return is shown by the sacrifice-fire simile, not by his motive. The 'grievance versus guarantee' contrast is the note's invention.

The shared act is refusing the philanderer's chest (பரத்தையர்த் தோய்ந்த மார்பம் ... தீண்டார் / நண்ணேன் பரத்த நின் மார்பு). But 2722 gives a charge in the mate's mouth, not a 'proved' infidelity, and the verse is flagged uncertain; the epic cannot test the couplet, and Kural 1311 is a playful ஊடல்.

1259 pitches camp on a hill and 1266 has the armies meet; that is story order. The camper in 1259 is unnamed (marker's own caveat) and 1266 gives a different epithet, so identifying them depends on the plot, and the verse does not answer or reverse the earlier one.

3033 is the bees' lament for hair and garland (கொங்குடைக் கோதை), and Siddhar 329 is a contented list of what the renouncer needs. These are not incompatible claims on one thing; the bees' complaint is a conceit that, by the marker, does not argue against renunciation. 'Cost of renunciation' is read in.

254 has the king thank his ministers for his kingship (என்னை நீர் இறைவன் ஆக்கி), not welcome unwanted counsel; 206 is a counsellor urging a king bent on pleasure. Two kings of different epics and different scenes are joined by the word 'counsel', and 'the ideal depends on a willing king' is not in 254.

714 has her vow to bind him with a garland (மாலையாலே ... யாப்பன்) in answer to his binding her heart (என் உள்ளம் யாத்தாய்); 738 has her fastening the golden garland on his chest (ஆகத்துப் பூட்டி). The later verse fulfils the vow in the same word யா-/பூட்டு, and the inward vow precedes the public act.

210 owns the trick: வன்பொறி யானை விட்டேன், and 39 shows the artificial elephant built of lac, thread, wood and hide (தாமியற்றினார்). 210 turns the trap into an offer to win the Kuru line, so the later verse explains the earlier device. The makers in 39 are unnamed, but the elephant is the same.

1167 has the hero meet prison and release with ஊழ்வினை என்று விட்டான்; 1172 has the god say he was relieved of his suffering as a dog (பிணிக்குலத்து ... நோய்கெடுத்து), so the 'former deed' behind the release is Civakan's own kindness. The pairing shows karma made visible to the reader, though the dog explains only the release, not the prison.

The two verses share the doe struck by a spear (எஃகு எறி பிணையின் மாழ்கி / வேலேறு பெற்ற பிணையின் மாழ்கி), but this is a stock simile, and the 'usurper's queen' is the marker's inference (the verse names no one). The 'wrong comes home' reading is an interpretation laid over a repeated formula.

The epic follows NL 17's argument in the Tamil: hair, brow, brows, eyes and nose go from praised likenesses to decay (வெண் மணல் ஆகிய கூந்தல், கழுநீர்க் கண் ... வழுநீர் சுமந்தன) and the speaker is Manimekalai herself, to Udayakumaran, while NL has a man warn men (வெஃகன்மின் மற்றிவளும் கோல்கண்ணளாகும்). Turning the lesson into her own refusal is true.
links.text_issue: LINK header carries no Gains line; gains_holds set to null

links.reason: 21 is the king's vow to offer a pair (யான் இவ் வாளினின் மக்களிரட்டையை ... பலியாக), and 32 is the brother's comfort to his sister (உடம்பிற் கேதம் எய்துவது ... நமதன்று). Neither contradicts the other: the brother does not dispute the rite, he consoles. The tension type does not fit; 32 answers 21 only as the victims' reply.

22 already has him crown the boy and give up his retinue (முடியுஞ் சூட்டி ... கொடுத்து) and resolve on asceticism; 23 is the kingdom handed over and the going into the forest. That is the next step of the same story, not a later unit that answers the earlier, and 22 has a damaged word.

1193 has swords drinking demons' blood to still their hunger, and 1199 has the plough working blood into mud and sowing victory; shared is blood and a weapon, but the images differ, and only 1199 is cultivation. 'The council's talk makes killing a work of cultivation' reads 1199's metaphor into 1193.

427 has கற்றவன் and சொல்ல வல்லனே; Kural 686 adds fearlessness and sense of time. 'The court has not yet asked' is an argument from the verse's silence, and the ministers' reply is only a nomination. It is an application of the Kural's first marks, not a development, and neither side gains something stated.

1508 lists a cakravartin's jewels, treasures, lands, cities and kings; Kural 381 lists six organs. The note's 'no ministers or fort' is argument from silence in a list of wealth, and the verse is flagged uncertain at line 4. The pair is a shared topic.

2988 has Civakan call the wives to cross old deeds (தொல்வினை நீத்த நீந்தி) to the world above, a Jain release; Kural 346 makes cutting 'I' and 'mine' the way to a world above the gods. Setting the Kural's condition on the epic is the note's addition; neither text offers the other's missing half, so 'each gives what the other leaves open' is thin.

467 is the city women's wonder (அண்ணலைத் தவத்திற் றந்தார்); 29 has Civakan as one who tasted nectar and no longer wants women, but it does not use தவம் at all. The 'turned against the hope' needs a word the second verse lacks, and a crowd's remark is not set against the narrator's.

445 makes counsellors the ruler's eyes; 641 shows a king ordering counsel. The claim that the order is formal, after he has already decided, rests on 634-640, which the packet does not show, and the marker doubts it. The verse itself says only that he told the counsellors to speak.

635 is the king's boast (மேருத் துளங்குமோ ... மானிடப் பேதைகள் ஆற்றலால்); NL 3 says kings who rode elephants fall when their deeds turn (ஏனை வினை உலப்ப வேறாகி வீழ்வர்). The quatrain says nothing of boasting, so that the boast precedes the fall is the note's inference, and the epic is not shown to fall here.

192's கயல் பொருவ is 'resemble carp' (பொருவு), not the 'fighting' கயல் of NL 44 (பொருகயல்), so the shared words are not the same word; and 192 is the narrator's plain portrait, not a view the quatrain contradicts. NL 44 is a renunciant's resolve; the pair makes no incompatible claim, and the epic's 'fall of the king' is read in.
links.text_issue: 192 கயல் பொருவ: reading of பொருவ as 'fight' is doubtful

links.reason: 22 line 2 ranks flesh-eating with others as painful (ஊனைத்தின் றூனைப் பெருக்குதல்), and Kural 251 argues from it to lost அருள். The shared image is true, but 'ranked above' is the note's reading of முன்னின்னா, and the pair mostly shows the same phrase in two books.

170 states a general rule (அறமின்றிப் பின்னை ஒன்றும் ... தீக்கதிப் பிறவிக் கஞ்சி); NL 85 names one deed and its fruit (பிறர்மனைமேல் சென்றாரே ... அலியாகி). That 85 'grounds a whole poem's moral' is untrue of 170, which names no adultery, so the epic adds nothing to the quatrain.

2502 is a conceit of a pearl necklace with a will of its own (தஞ்சுற்றம் வேண்டாத முலைக்கீழ் வாழ்வு), and NL 120 says deeds alone go with a person and the adorned body is useless. The verse neither praises adornment nor argues for it, so there is no incompatible claim; 'a counter-voice' is imposed on a descriptive verse.

304 has a courtier say that no king fails to obey (மன்னவ ரில்லை), and 690 has Tivittan answer: திறையினை மறுத்தவர் ... முயன்று கொள்கவே. The later scene refutes the earlier universal claim, which the note says.

138 has வெங்கண் யானை வேந்து இறைஞ்ச the father's victory, and 159 repeats the phrase for the daughter (வெங்கண் யானை ... வேந்தரே ... அடிமைத்தொழில்) with her smile as lance (நகை வேலினால்). The echo of wording makes the transfer of homage from sword to beauty a reading of the Tamil.

540 has the king hold the suitors in hope and hide his mind; 613 has the Avanti king arrive with other kings. The horoscope, the destined husband and 'unknowing escorts' are not in 613; it is an arrival scene. Whose city and why are put in by the note.

904 has the mother tell of the daughter's anger at Civakan's verdict (சீவகன் றிறத்திற் காய்ந்தாள்); 2077 has her say the man who made her powder lose has won her (சுண்ணம் வாட்டினன் ... கற்பிது). The later verse reverses the earlier grievance; the obscure 'பெருவளைப் பிட்டுக் காத்த' does not touch the link.

2911 bars even one false syllable (நொடியலோ ரெழுத்தும் பொய்யை) for the king, for fear of losing fame; Kural 292 allows a blameless good to make a falsehood count as truth (புரைதீர்ந்த நன்மை). The motives differ, fame versus benefit, and the epic's rule is advice to a king, not a ruling on the Kural's case. At best a loose contrast.

547 has Nami ask the serpent king Dharanan for wealth (செல்வ மண்மிசைப் பெறுவன்), not a yogi, and the verse does not show him getting it. The Tirumanthiram's ranking of asking against tapas is a different school's rule, and the epic does not need it; the note's 'in the presence of a yogi' is not in the verse.
